title: Moten's band, battles of bands and the riff behind One O'Clock Jump
summary: Moten's band played the Harlem against Ellington and built riffs on tunes like Moten's Swing; Saunders and DeMichael discuss where Basie's One O'Clock Jump riff came from.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Pardon me. So that was -- that was the way these sessions -- and then, they had a battle of bands in there. See, Benny Moten's band would play at the Harlem and they would have Duke Ellington's band. And then it was one of those things where -- you know, and Benny and them --

Benny Moten's band was the greatest band for just sitting down -- and they would start off a tune, this was tunes like "Moten's Swing" and all those things. And then they'd start to setting these riffs.
And this is where Basie got that thing, from "One O'Clock Jump." But he used to call that Old Babe, you know what I mean? And that was just a riff, you know?
Well, he told me about that bit. He claimed that it came from Louis Armstrong's recording of Stardust, when Louis sang, oh, memories, oh, memories.
Who knows? It was a standard riff back there, and they would go (singing), but it was that thing. And then Basie finally put it in that "One O'Clock Jump".
